use-after-free: Move the final read before cleanup, or extend the lifetime so cleanup happens after every user has finished. Follow the release note: freeing an alias invalidates the original pointer too. Assigning NULL to one variable does not repair other dangling aliases. An error means the object is released on every path to the use; a warning ("may have been freed") means some paths release it, so make the release and the use agree on every path. In a weavec-cc build a guard also stops such a use at run time while the freed block is still in the runtime's quarantine. See [your first check](/getting-started/first-check/).
double-free: Give each allocation one clear cleanup path. After ownership transfer, let the new owner release it. On error paths, track whether ownership actually transferred before local cleanup. Reference-counted objects need one release per acquired share. In a default weavec-cc build the runtime's allocator also validates every free: a second release of a block stops the program at run time, as long as the block's storage has not been reused.
use-after-move: Stop using the old owning pointer after transfer. Borrow the object when the callee only needs temporary access, or use a new value returned by the operation. With realloc, distinguish success from failure and avoid keeping aliases into the old storage after successful growth.
conflicting-borrow: Delay release, transfer, or mutation until the borrow's final use, or shorten the borrow by moving its last use earlier. If the copy is never used after the release (a failure path that leaves it in a struct the caller discards), clear it or ignore the warning; a use of it would be reported as use-after-free.
lifetime-too-short: Ensure the referent lives at least as long as every pointer that escapes. Return a value, use caller-provided storage, or allocate storage with an ownership contract instead of returning an address into a local stack frame.
unsafe-operation: Inspect why the pointer or call is raw. Prefer a modeled or verified interface with an accurate contract. If the operation necessarily crosses the supported model, put the smallest reviewed operation inside a WEAVEC_UNSAFE boundary and document the assumptions. Unsafe code still affects ownership outside the boundary, and weavec-cc does not guard its accesses.
mismatched-release: Pair the resource with its allocator's release family: malloc with free, fopen with fclose, and opendir with closedir. For a custom family, express the contract with WEAVEC_OWNED and WEAVEC_OWNED_BY and ensure wrapper bodies agree.
leak: Release or transfer the owned resource on every applicable exit path. Before overwriting an owning pointer, dispose of the old resource. Free owned child allocations before their container. A shared cleanup label can make C error paths easier to audit.
null-dereference: Check nullable results before their first use and keep that condition on every path reaching the dereference. The error means the pointer is null on every path from a non-allocator source. A pointer that may be null is not reported; in a weavec-cc build a guard stops a null dereference at run time. Propagate allocation or lookup failure to callers when appropriate. Use WEAVEC_NONNULL only for an interface whose callers can establish the requirement.
use-of-uninitialized: Initialize the pointer or record field on every path before reading it. A declaration alone does not establish a value. The error means no path assigns it first. weavec-cc zero-initializes locals, so a pointer that may be uninitialized is null instead, and a guard stops its dereference at run time.
invalid-release: Release the original allocation base with the correct releaser. Stack objects, string literals, and interior pointers are not independently freeable. Keep the owning base separate from traversal cursors. In a default weavec-cc build the runtime's allocator also validates every free: releasing an interior pointer, a pointer to a stack or global object, or a block that was already released stops the program at run time.
out-of-bounds: Compare the access against the actual allocation size, including element size and space for string terminators. Array indices must be smaller than the element count. Establish and preserve bounds across calls; a capacity field does not enlarge the allocation it describes. The error means the access fails for every value the analysis allows against an exact extent; an access that only may overrun is not reported. In a weavec-cc build a guard stops an access that leaves its object at run time.
invalid-integer-operation: Validate operands before the operation: divisors must be nonzero, shifts must have valid counts, signed results must be representable, and VLA dimensions must be positive. Check multiplication and conversion before using a result as an allocation size. See [integers and bounds](/guides/integers-and-bounds/).
annotation-mismatch: Compare the annotation with the function body and its callers. Correct the implementation or the declared contract so they describe the same ownership, extent, and effects. Do not strengthen an annotation simply to silence a diagnostic.
invalid-annotation: Check the macro spelling, placement, supported declaration kind, and named parameters or fields. WEAVEC_COUNTED_BY and WEAVEC_SIZED_BY must name a sibling integer parameter or field, WEAVEC_ENDED_BY a sibling pointer, and WEAVEC_OWNED_BY requires WEAVEC_OWNED. See [annotation placement](/reference/annotation-placement/).
contradicted-assumption: The assumption is false on the path the note describes, so what the analysis concludes after it rests on a false premise. Fix the code that makes the value violate the assumption, or correct the assumption to what the code guarantees. Do not weaken an assumption only to silence the error. Nothing checks an assumption at run time: one the analysis cannot decide is simply assumed.
allocation-failure: Test the allocation's result before its first use and handle the failure, for example by returning an error or calling an abort routine. The warning is off by default because a weavec-cc build already traps on the null dereference; enable it to find the places that should report the failure gracefully.
